[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''James Glasgow''' was reportedly born in '''1737'''. A Larne or Kilwaughter congregational record is said to contain an entry for a James, son of [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]], at '''New Town, Larne''', in that year.

The original congregational entry, or a reliable full transcription, has not yet been cited on this profile. The exact birth date, place and identification of Hugh as James’s father should therefore be treated as probable rather than conclusively established.

James was a '''ropemaker''' at Larne, County Antrim. A lease dated 10 September 1760, registered on 24 November 1763, describes him as a ropemaker of Belfast and leases him a marked-out ropewalk at Gardenmore in Larne for thirty-one years from 1 November 1760. He agreed to build a house at the south end of the ropewalk.<ref name="Ropewalk1760">Registry of Deeds transcript, lease dated 10 September 1760 and registered 24 November 1763, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-S7XZ-8 FamilySearch image].</ref>

On 28 March 1768 James, described as a ropemaker of the Old Town of Larne, assigned the plot, workhouse and remainder of the same lease to John Hill for £50. The matching commencement date and rent identify it as the 1760 ropewalk.<ref name="Ropewalk1768">Registry of Deeds transcript, assignment dated 28 March 1768, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-DDXW FamilySearch image].</ref>


A memorial at '''St Cedma’s Church, Larne''', is reported to record James Glasgow with the dates '''1737–1802''' and to name his wife as '''Janet Shutter'''. A photograph or complete reliable transcription of the monument should be cited before the exact dates and marriage are treated as fully verified.

James is reported to have died in '''1802'''.

An Irish probate-index transcription records a '''James Glasgow of Larne''' in the Diocese of Belfast in '''1803'''.<ref>Irish probate index transcription supplied July 2026, entry for James Glasgow, Diocese of Belfast, residence Larne, 1803.</ref>

The agreement in name and residence, together with probate in the year after the reported death, makes this a strong match to the man commemorated at St Cedma’s.

The 1803 entry should be understood as a probate or estate event. It does not replace the reported 1802 death year. Probate occurring in the year following death would be ordinary.

The probate entry establishes Larne as James’s recorded residence during the estate proceedings. It does not by itself prove that Larne was his place of death.

=== Wife and family ===

James’s wife is reported on the St Cedma’s memorial as '''Janet Shutter'''.

The complete inscription should be obtained and cited because the memorial may also contain:

* Janet’s dates;
* the date or duration of the marriage;
* children buried in the same plot;
* other Glasgow relatives; or
* wording clarifying whether the monument was erected by descendants.

No inspected baptismal, marriage, will or probate record currently cited on this profile names James’s children.

The 1803 probate record may be important. An original will, administration bond or surviving abstract could identify:

* Janet as his widow;
* sons or daughters;
* married daughters or sons-in-law;
* executors or administrators;
* business partners;
* property at Larne or Blackcave; or
* other relatives.

== Research Notes ==

=== John of Inishrush: dependent son hypothesis — 17 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-822|John Glasgow]], born on 10 April 1767 according to his family Bible, is selected as James’s '''very uncertain possible son, 18% subjective probability'''. The proposal extends James’s existing uncertain fatherhood of [[Glasgow-3902|Adam Glasgow]] through the preferred but unproved Adam/John brother comparison. Adam and John were nine years apart, headed separate Inishrush households in 1831, and shared a close family/community news network: John’s 1847 letter discusses the younger James Glasgow/Henry Barkly family associated with Adam’s descendants. James occurs in both branches’ names.<ref>[https://hiltner.com/mckeown/getperson.php?personID=I368&tree=tree1 John Glasgow family-register account], with reviewed Bible images; [https://www.hiltner.com/mckeown/documents/John%20Glasgow%20letter%20to%20Jane%20Glasgow%20Gray%203-20-1847.pdf John’s letter to Jane Glasgow Gray, 20 March 1847]; [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/Tamlaght/1831census_3.html 1831 Tamlaght O’Crilly census transcription], John at house2, entry1019, Adam separately at house91; [https://www.oneirishrover.com/tamlaght-graveyard/ Adam’s monument], died 30 June 1844 aged86. Denomination disagreements remain unresolved.</ref>

This 18% father selection is weaker than the existing 27% James–Adam hypothesis. It depends both on that father model and on brotherhood; neither assumption independently confirms the other. Cousinship remains possible. John’s sons Adam–James–John and daughters beginning Rose–Maria favour an older Adam/Maria reconstruction as a substantial unnamed rival. No extra person is invented. James’s 1760 ropewalk lease and 1773 age affidavit establish a compatible Larne adult, not migration or paternity.<ref name="Ropewalk1760" /><ref name="Larne1773" />

[[Shutter-46|Janet Shutter]] is not assigned as John’s mother. John’s 94% identity comparison with the 1831 householder represented by [[Glasgow-3927]] is separately assessed and does not validate that account’s placeholder ancestry. James’s own parentage, existing children and the older Alexander hypothesis retain their grades. John’s selected placement is a new, deliberately weak working connection; no brotherhood or fatherhood is established by a contemporary parent record.


=== Selected uncertain family — 16 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-1509]], the older Larne ropemaker, is selected as the uncertain working father of Adam of Inishrush ([[Glasgow-3902]]). This adopts the named-family comparison already tested in September. Adam’s gravestone age implies birth about 1758; James’s reported 1737 birth would give an ordinary age-21 generation. The original 1773 affidavit independently places the Larne James’s birth before October 1743, although it does not prove the reported 1737 year. Adam’s proved son James ([[Glasgow-3903]]) supplies limited positive naming support. James is a documented adult with a trade and property trail, making him a more useful provisional father than the recordless [[Glasgow-3905]] placeholder. No record names Adam as his child, and the naming argument is weak rather than corroboration of a parent clause.

The same James is selected, with very low confidence, as father of the reconstructed older Alexander ([[Glasgow-3904]]). This adopts the existing possible-brother route for Adam and Alexander. On the reported 1737 and estimated 1770 years, James would be about 33 at Alexander’s birth. Making Adam, born about 1758, Alexander’s father instead produces a twelve-year interval. Alexander’s circa 1770 birth is only an estimate, so that calculation does not exclude an Adam father: Alexander could have been born later. However, fatherhood of Daniel by about 1795/96 places Alexander in a generation born by roughly 1775–1778, leaving two short successive generations in the Adam-to-Alexander model. Adam’s wife [[Unknown-760890]], born about 1766/67 from her monument age, cannot be Alexander’s mother on that chronology. The sibling route is therefore preferred provisionally without inventing an earlier wife. Chronological economy does not prove brotherhood or a shared father; neither selected edge is independent support for the other.

A 1760 lease identifies James as a Belfast ropemaker taking a ropewalk at Gardenmore, Larne; the 1768 assignment identifies the same property. This is a real occupational and locality sequence, distinct from the contemporary Larne tanner. Adam is documented much later at Inishrush, and the monument does not state his birthplace. The estimated Inishrush birth cannot exclude a family from elsewhere, but no Belfast birth or Larne-to-Inishrush migration is newly assigned. The 1773 Larne gentleman’s age excludes the younger [[Glasgow-3991]] account; the identity assessment and separation of the two trades retain their previous grades. The reported James/[[Shutter-46]] marriage in 1762 is later than Adam’s birth. It cannot establish [[Shutter-46]] as Adam’s mother. An earlier union, premarital birth or inaccurate reported date would be needed if this father model is right; no such event or person is invented. [[Shutter-46]] is not selected as older Alexander’s mother either: the marriage report and the son identity are independently unproved.

The two local 1740 Tamlaght Hugh households, including [[Glasgow-3931]], and the older Adam-and-Maria naming model remain alternatives for Adam. A different unrecorded father remains possible. Neither Larne property succession nor the Inishrush household totals connect these generations. The 1831 return does not identify its unnamed occupants, and the later plot-29 succession is not evidence of James the ropemaker’s paternity. The shared [[Glasgow-3905]] field is a recently created research placeholder, not evidence that Adam, older Alexander and [[Glasgow-1367]] were brothers. It is not identified or merged with James. No father is extended to [[Glasgow-1367]], and no unnamed extra generation is added.

Older Alexander is himself reconstructed chiefly from late descendant testimony naming Thomas’s parents as Alexander and Rosanna. The 2007 account and its copied 2020 restatement are one source tradition, not independent witnesses. Daniel and Thomas are proved brothers, but their father’s name is not established by a contemporary parent record. The new James father therefore depends on that reconstructed older Alexander account. Younger [[Glasgow-951]] remains a separate, unresolved possible brother or cousin of Thomas and Daniel; the record-defined [[Glasgow-4090]] remains his leading current father comparison. This batch does not select older Alexander as younger Alexander’s father or place that younger family beneath James. No Rosanna surname or October 1822 death date is newly established. James’s own [[Glasgow-1505]] and [[Glasgow-1499]] ancestry alternatives and existing children retain their earlier assessments.

The proposed fathers remain unproved, and neither mother is identified by this reconstruction. [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/branches/larne-kilwaughter/#larne-inishrush-working-family Full selected model, competing families and source limits]. <ref>Existing reviewed records and public profile citations: [https://www.oneirishrover.com/tamlaght-graveyard/ Tamlaght gravestone: Adam died 30 June 1844 aged 86; Rose died 31 July 1833 aged 66; photograph and transcription]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-S7XZ-8 Registry of Deeds, ropewalk lease 10 September 1760, registered 24 November 1763: Belfast ropemaker taking Gardenmore, Larne]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-DDXW Registry of Deeds, assignment 28 March 1768: matching Larne ropewalk and lease term]; [https://www.irishdeedsindex.net/mem.php?memorial=204122 Registry memorial 204122, 14 May 1766: James Glasgow, Larne ropemaker, witness]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-M72W-M Registry affidavit sworn 27 October 1773, registered 15 November: Larne gentleman aged upwards of thirty]; [https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 Genes Reunited thread 465937: 2007 descendant account, later copied; previously reviewed derivative testimony, not contemporary proof]; [https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740religiousreturnsulstername.pdf 1740 Protestant Householders’ Return, Macafee transcription: two Tamlaght Hugh households, no stated kinship]. These sources document the adults or late family testimony; they do not state the selected father relationships.</ref>


=== Identification and evidence ===

The following records probably concern the same man:

* the James, son of Hugh Glasgow, reportedly recorded at New Town or Larne in 1737;
* James Glasgow, ropemaker, documented in the 1760 ropewalk lease and 1768 assignment;
* James Glasgow commemorated at St Cedma’s with dates 1737–1802 and wife Janet Shutter; and
* James Glasgow of Larne whose estate entered Belfast probate in 1803.

The chronology and repeated Larne association make this identification plausible and probably correct.

The strongest direct contemporary evidence presently cited is the 1760 ropewalk lease and its 1768 assignment. The baptism and memorial evidence still require complete source citations, and the probate index does not name James’s father or wife.

The profile should therefore distinguish between:

* directly documented facts, including James’s ropemaking and Larne residence in the 1760–1773 records;
* strong identity matches, including the 1803 probate entry; and
* reported but not yet fully exposed evidence, including the 1737 congregational entry and St Cedma’s memorial.

=== Ropemaker evidence and identity distinction ===

A Registry of Deeds memorial dated 14 May 1766 also names James Glasgow, ropemaker of Larne, as a witness.<ref>[https://www.irishdeedsindex.net/mem.php?memorial=204122 Registry of Deeds Index Project, memorial 204122], deed dated 14 May 1766.</ref> In 1773 Mr James Glasgow of Larne, gentleman, swore that he was aged upwards of thirty, placing his birth before 27 October 1743.<ref name="Larne1773">Registry of Deeds memorial and affidavit, sworn 27 October 1773, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-M72W-M FamilySearch image].</ref> Alexander Holmes's 1799 will later identifies a Larne occupant as James Glasgow, roper. The repeated occupation and place form a coherent sequence.

The 1768 assignment was witnessed by a '''different''' James Glasgow who was expressly described as a tanner. A 1778 mortgage and the 1786 Blackcave lease continue that tanner sequence and fit [[Glasgow-3991|James Glasgow (about 1747–1812)]]. The two tradesmen should not be conflated.

The reported 1737 congregational occurrence and the present uncertain placement under [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]] remain competing parentage hypotheses until the original entry or another relationship record is inspected.

=== Research priorities ===

Further research should obtain:

* the original or fullest available congregational entry for the 1737 James, son of Hugh Glasgow;
* the name of the congregation and exact wording of that entry;
* a photograph or complete transcription of the St Cedma’s memorial;
* evidence supporting Janet Shutter’s identity and marriage to James;
* the exact nature of the 1803 Belfast probate entry;
* the original will, administration record or bond, if it survives;
* a Betham or other pre-destruction abstract of the estate;
* names of beneficiaries, executors, witnesses or sureties; and
* records identifying any children of James and Janet.

=== Research conclusion ===

James Glasgow was directly recorded as a ropemaker in the 1760 Larne ropewalk lease, the 1766 memorial and the 1768 assignment.

The 1803 Belfast probate entry for James Glasgow of Larne is a strong match to the man reportedly commemorated at St Cedma’s with dates 1737–1802. It supports Larne as his probate residence while remaining consistent with death in 1802.

The reported identification of his wife as Janet Shutter and his father as Hugh Glasgow is plausible, but the complete memorial and congregational record should be cited before those relationships and the exact dates are treated as certain.

=== Current Larne reconstruction ===

James is securely the Belfast/Larne ropemaker in the 1760 Gardenmore ropewalk lease and its 1768 assignment, and the 1773 affidavit places that adult James at Larne and over thirty. The 1768 document separately calls its witness James Glasgow a tanner; that is a different occupational record group, probably [[Glasgow-3991|James Glasgow]], and does not change this James's occupation. The original 1784 lease registered in 1790 has now been inspected: its witness is explicitly a tanner and belongs to the separate occupational sequence probably represented by [[Glasgow-3991|James Glasgow]]. James is a plausible earlier-generation candidate in the Larne reconstruction, including as a possible father of [[Glasgow-3902|Adam Glasgow]] and possible kin of [[Glasgow-3904|older Alexander Glasgow]], but no record yet makes either relationship. His 1762 marriage to Janet Shutter postdates Adam's estimated 1758 birth, so Janet cannot be called Adam's mother. A William Glasgow, merchant, witnessed the 1760 lease, but is not yet definitely [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]].<ref name="LarneCurrent">Registry of Deeds memorials for the 1760 lease, 1768 assignment and 1773 affidavit, cited above.</ref>

=== Additional source context ===

These contextual and comparison sources supplement the individual record assessments above; they do not supply a missing parental statement.
* Related profile: [[Glasgow-1509]].
<ref name="Retained2">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ4-4SJF Registry of Deeds, 1784 transaction registered in 1790: James Glasgow, tanner; sworn 17 August and registered 23 August 1790].</ref>


A lease dated 14 January 1784 was witnessed by James Glasgow of Larne, '''tanner''', with Samuel Drummond, merchant, and James Farries, writing clerk. James’s affidavit was sworn 17 August 1790; the memorial was registered on 23 August. The original reads “Tanner”, resolving an earlier automated “Turner” reading. This strengthens the occupational sequence, without independently naming his family.<ref name="Tanner1784">Registry of Deeds, memorial 278037, lease 14 January 1784, sworn 17 August and registered 23 August 1790, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ4-4SJF FamilySearch image 437], original inspected 21 September 2026. The online collection label 1734–1736 does not describe this image’s date.</ref>

=== Newtown title succession: identities unresolved ===

An 1874 deed recites a lease to James Glasgow dated 2 October 1779 and its renewal to Anne Glasgow and Jane Glasgow on 25 February 1832. The north-side Newtown property, formerly John English’s, adjoined a tenement formerly Hugh Glasgow’s. This documents succession to a lease, but does not call the women James’s daughters or identify which James held it. The monument wife Jane of [[Glasgow-3991|James Glasgow]] died in 1820 and cannot automatically be the 1832 Jane. [[Glasgow-3992|Ann Glasgow]], whose monument gives a May 1832 death, is only a candidate for Anne; the original renewal is needed.<ref name="Newtown1874">Registry of Deeds, Antrim to John Mulvenna, indenture 25 March 1874, registered 24 August 1874, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS54-77Q4-H FamilySearch image 475], recital inspected in the original; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS54-77QC-T continuation image 476].</ref>

A possible identification concerns James Glasgow. An 1874 indenture traces James Glasgow’s 2 October 1779 Newtown of Larne lease to a 25 February 1832 renewal to Anne and Jane Glasgow.<ref>Inspected historical source; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS54-77Q4-H record].</ref> Original recital inspected. It establishes title succession, not stated descent; James and both women’s identities remain unresolved. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns James Glasgow. The separate memorial 173108 records James Glasgow, ropemaker, assigning a messuage to John Hill on 28 March 1768; its witnessing James Glasgow is described as farmer.<ref>Inspected historical source; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-DDD6 record]; Inspected historical source; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-DDDL record].</ref> Original occupation checked. The same-day ropewalk and messuage assignments are different instruments. Whether the farmer and tanner witnesses are one man is unresolved. The identification remains uncertain.
